extracted.intended_audience: poets and prose writers applying to the Community of Writers summer workshops / conference
extracted.subtask_description: Information and application requirements for attending the Community of Writers summer workshops in poetry, fiction, and nonfiction (dates, submission materials, fees, tuition, lodging, accessibility, and faculty/publishing participation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop dates and program split
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry workshop runs June 22 to June 28; fiction and nonfiction (including creative nonfiction) run July 10 to July 17 in Olympic Valley, near Lake Tahoe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates determine which workshop to apply for and which faculty/programming you will access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program components / activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The program features workshops, craft talks, publishing panels, readings, and one-on-one conferences with faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect a mix of group workshops and individual conferences; plan submissions and goals accordingly (e.g., workshop-ready pages, desire for editorial feedback, networking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission materials — poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply, writers submitted four to five pages of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a $35 application fee; adhere to the March 10 deadline; see the website for the application form and complete guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission materials — prose
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply, writers submitted up to 5,000 words of prose (for fiction or nonfiction applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a $40 application fee; adhere to the March 10 deadline; visit the website for the application form and complete guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fees and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Application fees are $35 for poetry and $40 for prose; submissions were due by March 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm current fees and deadline on the program website; payment and timely submission are required for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition and inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition is $1,725 for a poetry workshop and $1,850 for a prose workshop; tuition includes some meals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for tuition plus separate lodging costs; check website or program staff for what meals are covered and refund/cancellation policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lodging options and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Lodging available in private or shared condos as well as nearby shared houses; prices ranged from $80 per night for a shared bunkroom in a house to $285 per night for a private one-bedroom condo; prices vary slightly for poetry and prose workshop attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan travel and lodging budget separately from tuition; availability and exact pricing may change—confirm when registering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarships and financial aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-tuition scholarships and financial aid designated for underrepresented writers were available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants seeking funding should consult the program website or contact staff for eligibility, application process, and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty and teaching caliber
rubrics_metrics.description: The faculty includes named poets, fiction, and nonfiction writers (e.g., Kazim Ali, Brenda Hillman, Amy Tan, Monica West, Héctor Tobar, etc.), indicating the program's teaching roster and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty list is a signal of program focus and prestige; applicants may tailor submissions or goals based on the faculty’s strengths and specializations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing professionals and networking opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating publishing professionals include editors (e.g., Tara Parsons, Todd Portnowitz), editors of literary journals (e.g., Andrew Tonkovich, Oscar Villalon, Blaise Zerega), and agents (e.g., Michael V. Carlisle, Michael Mungiello, Lucy Carson, BJ Robbins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities to meet editors and agents are part of the program; applicants seeking publishing guidance should prepare materials and questions for panels and one-on-one interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility accommodations include accessible sidewalks, pathways, and doorways; accessible bathrooms; accessible parking; closed captioning for online programming; transcriptions of talks; venue signage in Braille; and interpretive listening devices (with advance request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the executive director via phone or e-mail for additional accessibility details and to request specific accommodations in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and application resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact: Community of Writers, P.O. Box 1416, Nevada City, CA 95959. (530) 470-8440. Brett Hall Jones, Executive Director. Website: https://communityofwriters.org
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit the website for the application form and complete guidelines; use the provided contact information for questions about the program, application, accessibility, and lodging.
